mainEntity.name: How does replacing water-damaged ceiling drywall differ from repairing wall drywall?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ceiling drywall poses a severe collapse danger when saturated, whereas wall drywall primarily faces mold and stability concerns. Water pooling on top of ceiling board adds massive weight; gypsum dissolves under water, causing screws to tear through and panels to fall without warning. If your ceiling is sagging, bulging, or discolored, place a bucket underneath and carefully puncture the center with a screwdriver to relieve water weight before it tears down entire sheets. Saturated ceiling drywall almost always requires immediate replacement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ceilings pose immediate collapse hazards due to pooling water weight. They require draining, complete removal of sagging sections, and secured refastening to ceiling joists.
